reason: The text depicts Yahweh (אֱלֹהִים) as actively engaged and immanent rather than remote. God directly intervenes to reward the midwives who fear Him ('וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת' - 'And God dealt well with the midwives'), and the passage emphasizes that 'וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּים' (God made them houses). The midwives' fear of God ('וַתִּירֶאן הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִים') and God's direct blessing in response portrays a deity who is present, responsive, and personally invested in human affairs. This is the opposite of a remote deity; it emphasizes divine immanence and active moral engagement.
